Each step on a pile of $n \ge 2$ grains uses the smallest prime factor $p$ of $n$. She makes $n/p$ groups and eats one grain from each, so the pile drops from $n$ to $n - n/p$. When one grain remains, she eats it, and that is also a step.

Starting from $2401 = 7^4$:

| Step | Pile before | Smallest $p$ | Pile after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2401 | 7 | 2058 |
| 2 | 2058 | 2 | 1029 |
| 3 | 1029 | 3 | 686 |
| 4 | 686 | 2 | 343 |
| 5 | 343 | 7 | 294 |
| 6 | 294 | 2 | 147 |
| 7 | 147 | 3 | 98 |
| 8 | 98 | 2 | 49 |
| 9 | 49 | 7 | 42 |
| 10 | 42 | 2 | 21 |
| 11 | 21 | 3 | 14 |
| 12 | 14 | 2 | 7 |
| 13 | 7 | 7 | 6 |
| 14 | 6 | 2 | 3 |
| 15 | 3 | 3 | 2 |
| 16 | 2 | 2 | 1 |
| 17 | 1 | (eat the last grain) | 0 |

It takes 17 steps to finish all the rice.

ANSWER: 17
